analysis.notes: The AABA form in its purest state. The A section is I – II7#11 – ii – V – I: the D7#11 is a V7/V whose #11 (G#) rubs against the key, and it is the whole flavour of the tune. The second ending turns C6 into C7 (V7/IV) to reach the bridge in F. The bridge sits on Fmaj7 for four bars, then D7 (V7/ii) leads back to Dm7–G7 and the last A. Fast tempos are the norm, so comp economically.

learning.why: The archetypal AABA tune and the archetypal II7#11 chord. Also your first fast tune: learn to comp lightly and place notes rather than fill every beat.
concepts: AABA form with first and second endings
drills: Loop bars 3–4 and play D lydian dominant (D E F# G# A B C) against the D7#11.
Comp only on beats 2 and 4 for a whole chorus at 160 BPM, then 180.
Solo on the A section using the C major scale but playing G# on every D7#11.
Trade fours with the trio: four bars comping, four bars soloing.
milestones: Know the form and changes from memory
Comp shells through the form at 160 BPM
Comp drop-2 voicings with the trio
Play a chord-tone solo over the whole form
Play the melody from memory (learn it by ear from a recording)
